quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A team of paleoclimatologists reconstructing historical drought patterns from tree-ring data spanning eight centuries found that the most severe drought period in the reconstructed record, occurring several centuries before modern industrial record-keeping began, was of comparable or even greater severity and duration than any drought experienced within the era of direct meteorological measurement, a finding the team argued should temper claims that current drought conditions are unprecedented in an absolute historical sense, even as the researchers emphasized that today's droughts are unfolding within a very different context of far higher regional water demand, extensive groundwater depletion, and a much larger population dependent on increasingly strained water systems than existed during any historical drought captured in the tree-ring record.
options: While historical droughts may have matched or exceeded today's in raw severity, the researchers stress today's droughts occur in a context of far greater water demand and strain.
The researchers concluded that current droughts are entirely unprecedented in every respect.
Historical droughts were consistently milder than any drought in the modern meteorological record.
Water demand and population pressures were comparable throughout the entire eight-century record.
quests.correctAnswer: While historical droughts may have matched or exceeded today's in raw severity, the researchers stress today's droughts occur in a context of far greater water demand and strain.
quests.hint: Notice the two things the passage compares: raw drought severity versus the surrounding context of demand and population.
quests.explanation: The tree-ring record shows historical droughts matching or exceeding modern ones in raw severity, tempering claims of an unprecedented drought today, but the researchers stress that modern droughts unfold amid far greater water demand and population pressure, a crucial context the historical comparison alone doesn't capture.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A labor market researcher analyzing the long-term career trajectories of workers who experienced a significant layoff during a major economic downturn found that workers who accepted a lower-paying position within their same industry within six months of job loss ultimately achieved higher lifetime earnings than workers who held out for a longer period searching for a comparable-salary position, even accounting for the initial pay cut absorbed by the first group, a pattern the researcher attributed to the first group avoiding the resume gap and skill atrophy that tended to compound the longer displaced workers remained out of the workforce entirely, ultimately outweighing the short-term financial sacrifice of accepting a lower salary sooner.
options: Holding out for a comparable-salary position led to higher lifetime earnings.
The timing of returning to work had no bearing on lifetime earnings.
Accepting a lower-paying job sooner after layoff appears to lead to higher lifetime earnings than holding out longer, likely because it avoids compounding resume gaps and skill atrophy.
Both groups of workers ultimately achieved identical lifetime earnings.
quests.correctAnswer: Accepting a lower-paying job sooner after layoff appears to lead to higher lifetime earnings than holding out longer, likely because it avoids compounding resume gaps and skill atrophy.
quests.hint: Notice the mechanism the researcher offers for why the quicker-accepting group did better over the long run despite an initial pay cut.
quests.explanation: Workers who took a lower-paying job sooner ended up with higher lifetime earnings than those who held out, and the researcher attributes this to avoiding the compounding resume gap and skill atrophy of extended unemployment, which outweighed the initial pay cut over time.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: An art historian studying the reception of a once-controversial painting style found that critical opinion had shifted dramatically over the roughly seventy years since the style's introduction, moving from near-universal dismissal by contemporary critics, who characterized the work as amateurish and lacking technical skill, to widespread critical acclaim by the following generation of critics, who instead praised the same technical choices as deliberate and innovative departures from convention, a reversal the historian suggested illustrates how critical judgments of technical skill are not purely objective assessments but are shaped substantially by the prevailing artistic conventions and expectations of the era in which the judgment is being made.
options: The historian concluded that judgments of technical skill are entirely objective and unaffected by era.
Critical opinion of the style remained consistently negative across all seventy years.
The historian suggests that critical judgments of technical skill are shaped by the artistic conventions of their era rather than being purely objective.
The later generation of critics agreed entirely with the original contemporary critics' assessment.
quests.correctAnswer: The historian suggests that critical judgments of technical skill are shaped by the artistic conventions of their era rather than being purely objective.
quests.hint: Notice the broader conclusion the historian draws from this specific reversal in critical opinion.
quests.explanation: The same technical choices were dismissed by one generation and praised by the next, leading the historian to conclude that judgments of technical skill are shaped by the artistic conventions of a given era rather than representing a purely objective, unchanging standard.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A team of computer security researchers studying the long-term effectiveness of mandatory security awareness training found that employee susceptibility to simulated phishing attempts dropped sharply in the weeks immediately following each annual training session but gradually crept back upward over the following months, approaching pre-training susceptibility levels by roughly the tenth month, a decay pattern that led the researchers to argue that the standard model of infrequent, large-block annual training sessions may be fundamentally less effective at producing durable behavioral change than a model of smaller, more frequent training touchpoints distributed more evenly throughout the year, even if the total cumulative training time remained identical under both approaches.
options: Annual training's benefits appear to decay significantly over time, leading researchers to favor smaller, more frequent training touchpoints over a single large annual session.
Susceptibility to phishing remained low throughout the entire year after annual training.
The researchers concluded that annual training was clearly the more effective approach.
Total cumulative training time was the only factor that mattered, regardless of how it was distributed.
quests.correctAnswer: Annual training's benefits appear to decay significantly over time, leading researchers to favor smaller, more frequent training touchpoints over a single large annual session.
quests.hint: Notice the researchers' argument about distributing training differently, even with the same total amount of training time.
quests.explanation: Susceptibility dropped after training but crept back up over months, nearly returning to baseline, leading researchers to argue that spreading the same total training time across smaller, more frequent sessions might produce more durable results than one large annual block.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A health economist evaluating a state's expansion of telehealth coverage for mental health services found that overall utilization of mental health services increased substantially following the expansion, but a closer geographic analysis revealed that the increase was concentrated almost entirely in areas that already had reasonable access to in-person mental health providers, while historically underserved rural areas, the population telehealth expansion was specifically intended to help, saw only marginal increases in utilization, a gap the economist attributed to persistent barriers such as unreliable rural broadband access that telehealth coverage alone, without complementary infrastructure investment, could not fully overcome on its own, according to utilization data analyzed across every county in the state.
options: Underserved rural areas saw the largest increase in mental health service utilization.
Telehealth expansion appears to have mainly benefited areas that already had reasonable access, with limited reach into the underserved rural areas it was specifically intended to help.
Telehealth expansion had no measurable effect on mental health service utilization anywhere.
Broadband access had no bearing on how effectively telehealth expansion reached rural areas.
quests.correctAnswer: Telehealth expansion appears to have mainly benefited areas that already had reasonable access, with limited reach into the underserved rural areas it was specifically intended to help.
quests.hint: Notice which specific geographic areas showed the largest increase in utilization, and which showed only marginal gains.
quests.explanation: Utilization rose mainly in areas with existing access, while the underserved rural areas the policy specifically targeted saw only marginal gains, which the economist attributes to barriers like unreliable broadband that telehealth coverage alone couldn't overcome without additional infrastructure investment.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A behavioral economist studying charitable giving patterns found that donors who were offered a matching gift, in which a third party pledged to match their donation dollar-for-dollar, gave larger initial donations than donors offered no match, but longitudinal tracking of the same donors over the following three years revealed that matched donors were also somewhat less likely to continue giving to the same organization in subsequent years without a match being offered again, suggesting that matching gifts may be effective at maximizing a single donation's size while potentially undermining the kind of intrinsic motivation that sustains long-term, unprompted giving relationships with an organization.
options: Matching gifts increased both initial donations and long-term giving without further matches.
Donors offered no match gave larger initial donations than matched donors.
Matching gifts appear to boost initial donation size while potentially reducing donors' likelihood of continuing to give without a future match.
Whether a match was offered had no bearing on donors' subsequent giving behavior.
quests.correctAnswer: Matching gifts appear to boost initial donation size while potentially reducing donors' likelihood of continuing to give without a future match.
quests.hint: Compare the effect on initial donation size with the effect on giving in subsequent years without a match.
quests.explanation: Matched donors gave more initially but were less likely to keep giving without another match later, suggesting the matching incentive may boost a single donation's size at some cost to the kind of self-sustained motivation that keeps donors giving over the long term.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A researcher evaluating a statewide initiative that provided free graphing calculators to students in low-income school districts, intended to close a resource gap with wealthier districts where such devices were already common, found that standardized math scores in the participating districts did not improve significantly relative to comparison districts that did not receive the calculators, a null result the researcher attributed not to the devices themselves being unhelpful, but to insufficient accompanying teacher training on how to meaningfully integrate the calculators into instruction, since many teachers reported in surveys that they had received the devices with little to no guidance on adjusting their existing lesson plans to make effective use of them.
options: The researcher concluded the calculators themselves were fundamentally unhelpful for learning math.
Math scores improved substantially in the districts that received the free calculators.
Teachers reported receiving extensive training on integrating the calculators into their lessons.
The lack of score improvement appears attributable to insufficient teacher training in using the calculators, not to the devices themselves being unhelpful.
quests.correctAnswer: The lack of score improvement appears attributable to insufficient teacher training in using the calculators, not to the devices themselves being unhelpful.
quests.hint: Notice what the researcher specifically attributes the lack of improvement to, as opposed to what they explicitly rule out.
quests.explanation: Scores didn't improve, but the researcher explicitly attributes this to insufficient teacher training rather than the calculators being inherently unhelpful, since teachers reported getting little guidance on integrating the devices, suggesting the resource alone wasn't enough without proper instructional support.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: An environmental engineer studying green roof installations across a large city found that while green roofs reliably reduced building energy costs and stormwater runoff regardless of building height, their effect on reducing surrounding neighborhood air temperature, a benefit often cited in promotional materials, was measurable only for buildings under roughly six stories, since taller buildings' green roofs were simply too far removed from street level, where most human activity and heat exposure actually occurs, to meaningfully influence the temperature people on the ground actually experienced, even though the roofs themselves still provided their full building-level energy and stormwater benefits regardless of height.
options: Green roofs provided identical neighborhood cooling benefits regardless of building height.
Green roofs appear to reliably provide building-level benefits regardless of height, but their neighborhood-level cooling effect is limited mainly to shorter buildings closer to street level.
Taller buildings' green roofs provided no energy or stormwater benefits at all.
Building height had no bearing on any benefit provided by green roofs.
quests.correctAnswer: Green roofs appear to reliably provide building-level benefits regardless of height, but their neighborhood-level cooling effect is limited mainly to shorter buildings closer to street level.
quests.hint: Notice the passage distinguishes between building-level benefits and neighborhood-level cooling benefits, and how height affects each differently.
quests.explanation: Energy and stormwater benefits held regardless of building height, but the neighborhood cooling effect only showed up in shorter buildings, since taller buildings' roofs sit too far from street level to meaningfully affect the temperature people on the ground actually experience.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A tourism economist studying the long-term regional economic effects of hosting a major international sporting event found that host cities experienced a genuine short-term boost in tourism-related revenue during the event itself, but a comprehensive ten-year follow-up analysis found no statistically significant long-term increase in annual tourism visits compared to each city's pre-event trajectory, contradicting a commonly cited justification for public investment in hosting such events, that they generate a lasting 'global exposure' effect that meaningfully elevates a host city's status as an ongoing tourist destination well beyond the weeks the event itself was actually taking place.
options: The ten-year analysis confirmed a significant lasting increase in tourism from hosting the event.
The claimed long-term 'global exposure' benefit of hosting major sporting events does not appear supported by the ten-year data, despite a genuine short-term revenue boost.
The event provided no economic benefit to host cities at any point, even during the event itself.
The short-term and long-term tourism effects were identical in magnitude.
quests.correctAnswer: The claimed long-term 'global exposure' benefit of hosting major sporting events does not appear supported by the ten-year data, despite a genuine short-term revenue boost.
quests.hint: Notice the passage distinguishes between the genuine short-term boost and the commonly claimed long-term benefit.
quests.explanation: A real short-term tourism boost occurred during the event, but the ten-year data found no lasting increase afterward, directly contradicting the commonly cited claim that hosting such events produces a lasting global exposure benefit for the host city's tourism industry.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A developmental psychologist studying sibling relationships in early childhood found that children who were given explicit language for naming their emotions, such as being taught to say 'I feel frustrated' rather than simply crying or hitting when upset, showed measurably fewer physical conflicts with siblings over shared toys and space, but this effect was significant only in households where parents also consistently modeled using the same emotional vocabulary themselves during their own visible moments of frustration, with little measurable benefit observed in households where children learned the vocabulary in isolation without any accompanying parental modeling of the same language.
options: Teaching children emotional vocabulary appears to reduce sibling conflict mainly when parents also model that vocabulary themselves, not when taught in isolation.
The emotional vocabulary reduced conflict equally regardless of whether parents modeled it.
Parental modeling alone, without teaching children vocabulary, was most effective at reducing conflict.
The presence of emotional vocabulary had no bearing on sibling conflict in any household.
quests.correctAnswer: Teaching children emotional vocabulary appears to reduce sibling conflict mainly when parents also model that vocabulary themselves, not when taught in isolation.
quests.hint: Notice the specific condition under which teaching emotional vocabulary showed a measurable benefit.
quests.explanation: Emotional vocabulary reduced sibling conflict only in households where parents also modeled it themselves, with little effect when children learned it in isolation, suggesting the benefit depends on children seeing the vocabulary used, not simply being taught the words on their own.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A municipal researcher evaluating a pilot program that replaced traditional parking meters with a phone-based payment app across a downtown business district found that the app increased payment compliance and reduced the city's meter maintenance costs substantially, but a survey of downtown business owners revealed that elderly customers without smartphones, or without comfort using payment apps, reported avoiding the district more often after the change, even though the city had retained a small number of traditional coin-based meters specifically to accommodate this group, suggesting the mere availability of an alternative option was insufficient to fully offset the district's shift toward an app-centric parking experience.
options: Retaining some traditional meters was not enough to fully prevent elderly customers from avoiding the district after the shift toward app-based parking.
Elderly customers reported visiting the district more often after the app was introduced.
The city removed all traditional meters entirely, offering no alternative option.
The shift to app-based parking had no measurable effect on any group of customers.
quests.correctAnswer: Retaining some traditional meters was not enough to fully prevent elderly customers from avoiding the district after the shift toward app-based parking.
quests.hint: Notice that traditional meters remained available, yet a specific group still reported avoiding the district.
quests.explanation: Even though some traditional meters remained available, elderly customers uncomfortable with the app still reported avoiding the district more, suggesting that simply retaining an alternative option wasn't sufficient to offset the broader shift toward an app-centric experience for that group.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A sports psychologist studying pre-competition routines among elite gymnasts found that gymnasts who followed a highly specific, unvarying physical warm-up sequence before every competition reported lower pre-competition anxiety than gymnasts whose warm-up varied depending on the venue or circumstances, but when the psychologist examined actual competition scores, the two groups performed statistically identically, suggesting that while a rigid routine may offer genuine psychological comfort, it does not appear to translate into any measurable competitive advantage once gymnasts actually begin performing, at least within the specific population and competition level studied by the psychologist.
options: The rigid routine improved both anxiety levels and competition scores.
Gymnasts with varied warm-ups scored significantly better than those with rigid routines.
Warm-up routine type had no bearing on either anxiety levels or competition scores.
A rigid pre-competition routine appears to reduce anxiety without translating into any measurable improvement in actual competition performance.
quests.correctAnswer: A rigid pre-competition routine appears to reduce anxiety without translating into any measurable improvement in actual competition performance.
quests.hint: Notice the passage separates the effect on anxiety from the effect on actual competition scores.
quests.explanation: A rigid routine reduced anxiety, but competition scores were statistically identical between both groups, suggesting the psychological comfort of a fixed routine didn't translate into any measurable performance advantage once gymnasts actually competed.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A management researcher studying the rollout of a new performance review system that replaced annual ratings with continuous, informal feedback delivered throughout the year found that employee-reported clarity about performance expectations increased significantly under the new system, but managers reported the new system required substantially more of their weekly time investment than the old annual process had, a cost some managers described in interviews as unsustainable given their existing workload, prompting the researcher to note that the system's apparent success from an employee perspective may not be sustainable at scale without either reducing managers' other responsibilities or providing additional dedicated time for the ongoing feedback the new system requires.
options: The new system required less time investment from managers than the old process.
Employee clarity about expectations decreased under the new continuous feedback system.
The new feedback system appears to improve employee clarity, but its success may not be sustainable for managers without additional time or reduced other responsibilities.
Managers reported the new system was easily sustainable within their existing workload.
quests.correctAnswer: The new feedback system appears to improve employee clarity, but its success may not be sustainable for managers without additional time or reduced other responsibilities.
quests.hint: Notice the researcher's own caution about the system's sustainability, stated at the end of the passage.
quests.explanation: Employee clarity improved, but managers found the ongoing feedback demands unsustainable within their current workload, leading the researcher to caution that the system's apparent success might not hold at scale without addressing this time burden on managers.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A team of soil microbiologists studying the effects of a widely used agricultural fungicide on soil health found that while the fungicide effectively suppressed the specific crop-damaging fungus it was designed to target, it also produced a measurable, unintended reduction in populations of several beneficial soil fungi responsible for helping plant roots absorb nutrients, and this collateral reduction appeared to persist in treated soil for considerably longer, sometimes multiple growing seasons, than the fungicide's active suppression of the originally targeted pathogen, raising questions among the researchers about the treatment's true net long-term effect on overall soil and crop health beyond its narrow, short-term pest-control benefit.
options: The fungicide appears to cause longer-lasting harm to beneficial soil fungi than the duration of its intended benefit against the target pathogen, raising questions about its net long-term effect.
The fungicide's harm to beneficial fungi disappeared faster than its benefit against the target pathogen.
The fungicide had no measurable effect on any soil fungi besides the targeted pathogen.
Beneficial soil fungi populations were unaffected by the fungicide treatment.
quests.correctAnswer: The fungicide appears to cause longer-lasting harm to beneficial soil fungi than the duration of its intended benefit against the target pathogen, raising questions about its net long-term effect.
quests.hint: Compare how long the fungicide's harmful effect on beneficial fungi lasted versus how long its intended benefit lasted.
quests.explanation: The fungicide's unintended harm to beneficial fungi outlasted its intended suppression of the target pathogen, persisting across multiple growing seasons, which is why the researchers raise questions about whether the treatment's narrow short-term benefit is worth its longer-lasting collateral cost to overall soil health.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A food policy researcher studying the effects of a soda tax implemented in one city found that while overall soda purchases within city limits declined as intended following the tax's introduction, sales data from grocery stores located just outside the city boundary, but still within a short driving distance for many residents, increased by a nearly offsetting amount over the same period, suggesting that a meaningful share of the tax's apparent effect on consumption reflected residents simply shifting where they purchased soda rather than genuinely reducing how much soda they ultimately consumed overall, according to a regional analysis comparing sales data inside and outside the taxed boundary.
options: Soda purchases outside the city boundary also declined during the same period.
The tax caused a genuine reduction in overall soda consumption with no shift in purchasing location.
Sales data outside the city showed no meaningful change after the tax was introduced.
Much of the soda tax's apparent effect on consumption appears to reflect residents shifting where they bought soda rather than actually reducing how much they consumed.
quests.correctAnswer: Much of the soda tax's apparent effect on consumption appears to reflect residents shifting where they bought soda rather than actually reducing how much they consumed.
quests.hint: Compare what happened to soda sales inside the city with what happened to sales just outside the boundary.
quests.explanation: Sales fell inside the city but rose by a nearly offsetting amount just outside it, suggesting many residents simply drove a short distance to buy soda without the tax, rather than the tax genuinely reducing how much soda was ultimately being consumed overall.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A user experience researcher studying voice assistant adoption among older adults found that while initial onboarding sessions led by a human technician in the older adult's own home produced high rates of continued regular use six months later, the same onboarding content delivered remotely via video call, despite covering identical material and taking a comparable amount of time, produced substantially lower continued-use rates, suggesting that for this particular population, the physical presence of another person during initial setup may matter as much as the actual informational content being conveyed during that session.
options: For older adults, the physical presence of a technician during onboarding appears to matter as much as the informational content itself for encouraging continued use.
Remote video onboarding produced higher continued-use rates than in-person onboarding.
The onboarding method had no bearing on continued use rates among older adults.
In-person and remote onboarding covered substantially different content.
quests.correctAnswer: For older adults, the physical presence of a technician during onboarding appears to matter as much as the informational content itself for encouraging continued use.
quests.hint: Notice that the content and time were the same in both cases; only the physical presence of the technician differed.
quests.explanation: In-person onboarding led to more continued use than remote onboarding despite identical content, suggesting that for older adults specifically, having another person physically present during setup may matter just as much as what was actually taught during the session.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A sociolinguist studying the evolution of a regional dialect over three generations within the same family lineage found that while the grandparents' generation spoke the dialect as their primary everyday language and the grandchildren's generation used it only occasionally in specific family contexts, the grandchildren nonetheless demonstrated a more explicit, conscious knowledge of the dialect's grammatical rules than either of the two older generations, who had acquired the dialect implicitly through immersion and could use it fluently without being able to clearly articulate its underlying grammatical structure when directly asked to explain the reasoning behind a particular construction they used instinctively and correctly.
options: The grandparents' generation demonstrated the most explicit grammatical knowledge of the dialect.
The youngest generation appears to have gained explicit grammatical knowledge of the dialect even while using it less often than their fluent but implicitly-taught grandparents.
Fluency in daily use and explicit grammatical knowledge were found to be identical across all three generations.
The grandchildren used the dialect as their primary everyday language.
quests.correctAnswer: The youngest generation appears to have gained explicit grammatical knowledge of the dialect even while using it less often than their fluent but implicitly-taught grandparents.
quests.hint: Notice the distinction the passage draws between using a dialect fluently and being able to explain its grammar explicitly.
quests.explanation: The grandchildren used the dialect less often but understood its grammar more explicitly than their more fluent grandparents, suggesting that everyday fluency and conscious grammatical knowledge are separate things, likely because the grandchildren learned the dialect more formally rather than through pure immersion.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A clinical researcher studying patient adherence to a multi-drug regimen for a chronic condition found that patients who used a single combination pill containing all required medications adhered to their regimen significantly more consistently than patients prescribed the identical medications as separate individual pills, even though both regimens required an identical number of total pills taken per day and were covered by insurance at comparable out-of-pocket cost, suggesting that the cognitive and logistical simplicity of managing fewer distinct prescription bottles, rather than the total pill count itself, may be the more important factor driving adherence.
options: Total pill count was the primary factor determining medication adherence.
Patients on separate individual pills adhered more consistently than those on the combination pill.
The simplicity of managing fewer prescription bottles, rather than total pill count, appears to be the more important factor driving medication adherence.
Out-of-pocket cost was the primary factor explaining the difference in adherence.
quests.correctAnswer: The simplicity of managing fewer prescription bottles, rather than total pill count, appears to be the more important factor driving medication adherence.
quests.hint: Notice what stayed the same between the two groups (pill count, cost) and what differed (number of separate bottles).
quests.explanation: Both groups took the same number of pills at similar cost, yet the combination-pill group adhered more consistently, suggesting that managing fewer separate bottles, not the total pill count itself, is the more important factor behind the difference in adherence.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: An economist studying the effects of automatic annual rent increases tied to a fixed formula, as opposed to landlord-discretionary increases negotiated individually each year, found that tenants under the formula-based system reported significantly less housing-related stress in surveys, even in years when the formula-based increase was numerically larger than the median discretionary increase in comparable buildings that year, suggesting that predictability itself, the ability to anticipate and plan for a known increase well in advance, may matter more to tenants' sense of housing security than the actual magnitude of the increase they end up paying each year.
options: The magnitude of the rent increase was the only factor affecting tenant stress levels.
Predictability of rent increases appears to matter more to tenants' sense of security than the actual size of the increase.
Tenants under discretionary increases reported less stress than those under formula-based increases.
Predictability had no measurable relationship to tenants' reported housing stress.
quests.correctAnswer: Predictability of rent increases appears to matter more to tenants' sense of security than the actual size of the increase.
quests.hint: Notice that the formula-based increase was sometimes numerically larger, yet still associated with less stress.
quests.explanation: Tenants under predictable formula-based increases reported less stress even when the increase was numerically larger than discretionary increases elsewhere, suggesting that being able to anticipate and plan for a known change matters more to tenants' sense of security than the raw size of the increase itself.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A researcher studying the long-term effects of grade retention, holding a struggling student back to repeat a grade, found that retained students showed academic improvement relative to their own prior performance in the immediate year following retention, but when compared not to their own past performance but to a matched group of similarly struggling students who were instead promoted alongside their original age cohort and given additional targeted support services, the retained students showed no significant long-term academic advantage by high school, while reporting substantially higher rates of subsequent disengagement from school and eventual dropout.
options: Retained students showed a clear, lasting academic advantage over students given additional support instead.
Compared to similarly struggling students who received extra support without being held back, retained students showed no lasting academic advantage and worse long-term engagement outcomes.
Grade retention had no measurable effect on students' immediate academic performance.
Dropout rates were identical between retained students and students given additional support.
quests.correctAnswer: Compared to similarly struggling students who received extra support without being held back, retained students showed no lasting academic advantage and worse long-term engagement outcomes.
quests.hint: Notice the two different comparisons the passage makes: retained students against their own past performance, versus against a different comparison group.
quests.explanation: Retained students improved relative to their own past performance, but showed no advantage and worse dropout outcomes compared to similarly struggling students given support instead of retention, suggesting the right comparison group changes the conclusion about whether retention is genuinely beneficial long-term.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A conservation biologist studying reforestation efforts in a degraded tropical region found that plots reforested using a diverse mix of native species selected to mimic the original forest's structure required substantially more upfront cost and management expertise than plots reforested with a single fast-growing commercial timber species, but the native-species plots achieved measurably higher long-term carbon sequestration and supported substantially greater biodiversity recovery within twenty years, leading the biologist to argue that upfront cost comparisons alone, commonly used to justify cheaper single-species reforestation in policy discussions, dramatically understate the native approach's true long-term value once ecological outcomes are properly factored into the comparison.
options: Single-species reforestation achieved higher long-term carbon sequestration and biodiversity recovery.
Upfront cost was found to be the only meaningful factor in comparing reforestation approaches.
Upfront cost comparisons alone appear to understate the native-species approach's true long-term value once carbon sequestration and biodiversity outcomes are considered.
Native-species plots required less upfront cost and expertise than single-species plots.
quests.correctAnswer: Upfront cost comparisons alone appear to understate the native-species approach's true long-term value once carbon sequestration and biodiversity outcomes are considered.
quests.hint: Notice the biologist's argument about what upfront cost comparisons alone fail to capture.
quests.explanation: Native-species reforestation cost more upfront but delivered better long-term carbon and biodiversity outcomes, leading the biologist to argue that cost-only comparisons commonly used in policy discussions understate its true value once these longer-term ecological benefits are properly factored in.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A regional tourism board studying the effects of a new direct international flight route found that while total visitor numbers from the newly connected country increased substantially in the two years following the route's launch, average visitor spending per trip declined somewhat over the same period, a pattern the board's analysts attributed to the route attracting a broader range of travelers, including more budget-conscious visitors who previously found the destination inaccessible without a connecting flight, rather than the destination itself becoming less appealing to the kind of higher-spending visitor the route had originally been marketed toward attracting in the first place.
options: The destination became measurably less appealing to higher-spending visitors after the route launched.
Average visitor spending per trip increased after the new route was introduced.
Total visitor numbers declined after the new direct route was introduced.
The new route appears to have broadened the range of visitors, including more budget-conscious travelers, rather than making the destination less appealing to higher-spending visitors.
quests.correctAnswer: The new route appears to have broadened the range of visitors, including more budget-conscious travelers, rather than making the destination less appealing to higher-spending visitors.
quests.hint: Notice the analysts' explanation for the decline in average spending, and what they explicitly say it does not indicate.
quests.explanation: Visitor numbers rose while average spending per trip fell, and analysts attribute this to the route attracting a broader, more budget-conscious range of travelers rather than to the destination losing appeal among the higher-spending visitors it was originally marketed toward.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A family researcher studying households that adopted a rule against discussing work-related stress at the dinner table, in an effort to protect family time, found that while dinner-table conversation quality did improve for most surveyed families under the new rule, roughly a fifth of families later abandoned the rule entirely, reporting that suppressing work stress at dinner simply displaced those conversations to later in the evening, often after children had gone to bed, which some parents felt reduced opportunities for children to witness healthy modeling of how adults process and discuss workplace difficulties.
options: For most families the rule improved dinner conversation, but some found it simply displaced stress discussions to a time children no longer witnessed.
Every family that adopted the rule continued following it without exception.
The rule had no effect on dinner-table conversation quality for any family.
Families who abandoned the rule reported no reason for doing so.
quests.correctAnswer: For most families the rule improved dinner conversation, but some found it simply displaced stress discussions to a time children no longer witnessed.
quests.hint: Notice the passage describes a general improvement alongside a specific reason some families abandoned the rule.
quests.explanation: Most families saw improved dinner conversation, but a fifth abandoned the rule because it simply pushed stress discussions later, past children's bedtime, removing a chance for kids to see healthy modeling of how adults handle work difficulties, a cost some parents ultimately weighed against the rule's benefit.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A sports economist studying attendance patterns at minor league baseball games found that promotional giveaway nights, such as free bobblehead figurines, reliably boosted single-game attendance substantially above a team's seasonal average, but season-long attendance totals for teams that scheduled many giveaway nights were not meaningfully higher than totals for teams that scheduled few, since fans attracted primarily by a specific promotion tended to attend that single game and no others, rather than being converted into more frequent attendees who would return for non-promotional games throughout the remainder of the season.
options: Giveaway promotions appear to boost single-game attendance without meaningfully increasing a team's total season attendance, since promotion-driven fans rarely return for other games.
Teams with more giveaway nights saw meaningfully higher total season attendance.
Giveaway nights had no measurable effect on attendance for any single game.
Fans attracted by promotions consistently returned for non-promotional games throughout the season.

quests.hint: Compare the effect on a single promotional game's attendance with the effect on total season attendance.
quests.explanation: Giveaways boosted attendance for that specific game but didn't meaningfully raise season totals, since fans drawn by a promotion tended not to return afterward, suggesting the boost was a one-time draw rather than a genuine conversion into more frequent, ongoing attendees.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A public administration researcher studying participatory governance found that neighborhood councils granted genuine binding authority over a portion of local spending decisions saw substantially higher and more sustained resident participation over a five-year period than neighborhood councils that were purely advisory, offering only non-binding recommendations to city officials who retained full final authority, suggesting that residents' willingness to invest ongoing time and effort in civic participation may depend heavily on whether their involvement carries genuine decision-making weight rather than serving a primarily symbolic or consultative function within the broader governance structure.
options: Purely advisory councils saw higher sustained participation than councils with binding authority.
The type of authority granted to a council had no bearing on participation levels.
Participation levels were identical regardless of whether councils had binding authority.
Sustained resident participation appears to depend on councils having genuine binding authority rather than a purely advisory, symbolic role.
quests.correctAnswer: Sustained resident participation appears to depend on councils having genuine binding authority rather than a purely advisory, symbolic role.
quests.hint: Compare participation levels between councils with genuine binding authority and councils that were purely advisory.
quests.explanation: Councils with real binding authority sustained higher participation over five years than purely advisory councils, suggesting residents invest ongoing effort mainly when their involvement carries genuine decision-making weight rather than serving a merely symbolic or consultative role.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A team of computer scientists studying the energy efficiency of different data center cooling strategies found that while liquid immersion cooling, submerging servers directly in a specialized non-conductive fluid, achieved the lowest overall energy consumption per unit of computing power among all methods tested, its adoption across the industry remained limited primarily due to compatibility concerns with existing server hardware designed around traditional air cooling, meaning that realizing the technology's full efficiency potential at scale would likely require a broader, more costly hardware redesign across the industry rather than a simple retrofit of existing data center infrastructure already in operation.
options: Liquid immersion cooling could be easily adopted through a simple retrofit of existing hardware.
Liquid immersion cooling's efficiency advantage appears real, but realizing it at scale would likely require a broader hardware redesign rather than a simple retrofit.
Liquid immersion cooling showed the highest energy consumption among the methods tested.
Hardware compatibility had no bearing on the industry's adoption of liquid immersion cooling.
quests.correctAnswer: Liquid immersion cooling's efficiency advantage appears real, but realizing it at scale would likely require a broader hardware redesign rather than a simple retrofit.
quests.hint: Notice what the passage says would actually be required to realize the technology's full potential at scale.
quests.explanation: Liquid immersion cooling was the most efficient method tested, but the passage notes that existing hardware, built around air cooling, isn't compatible with it, meaning wider adoption would likely require costly redesign rather than being achievable through a simple retrofit of current infrastructure.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A team of geologists studying a series of moderate earthquakes along a previously little-monitored fault line found that the earthquakes' timing correlated closely with seasonal fluctuations in regional groundwater extraction for agricultural irrigation, with a disproportionate share of events occurring during the driest months when extraction rates peaked, leading the team to hypothesize that human-driven groundwater depletion may be altering stress conditions along the fault enough to influence the timing, though not necessarily the ultimate occurrence, of earthquakes that may have happened eventually regardless of any groundwater extraction taking place in the region.
options: The team concluded groundwater extraction is the sole cause of these earthquakes occurring at all.
Earthquake timing showed no relationship to seasonal groundwater extraction patterns.
Earthquakes occurred most often during the wettest months of lowest extraction.
Groundwater extraction may be influencing when these earthquakes occur, though not necessarily whether they occur at all.
quests.correctAnswer: Groundwater extraction may be influencing when these earthquakes occur, though not necessarily whether they occur at all.
quests.hint: Notice the specific distinction the passage draws between influencing timing and influencing whether an earthquake occurs at all.
quests.explanation: Earthquakes clustered during peak extraction months, leading researchers to hypothesize that extraction may shift the timing of earthquakes that were already likely to eventually occur, a more limited and careful claim than saying extraction directly causes earthquakes that otherwise wouldn't have happened.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A workplace researcher studying the adoption of four-day workweek pilots across multiple industries found that the practice produced the most consistent positive outcomes, in both employee wellbeing and maintained productivity, at companies that had already established strong existing processes for measuring output by results rather than hours logged, while companies that shifted to a four-day week without first developing such results-oriented measurement systems saw far more inconsistent outcomes, with some experiencing genuine productivity declines that the researcher attributed not to the shortened week itself but to the absence of a clear existing framework for evaluating whether work was actually getting done.
options: The shortened week itself was the primary cause of productivity declines wherever they occurred.
The four-day workweek appears most successful at companies that already measure output by results, with inconsistent outcomes elsewhere due to lacking such a framework, not the shorter week itself.
Companies without results-based measurement systems saw the most consistent positive outcomes.
The existing measurement system a company used had no bearing on the pilot's outcomes.
quests.correctAnswer: The four-day workweek appears most successful at companies that already measure output by results, with inconsistent outcomes elsewhere due to lacking such a framework, not the shorter week itself.
quests.hint: Notice what the researcher explicitly attributes productivity declines to, and what they explicitly rule out as the cause.
quests.explanation: Companies with existing results-based measurement saw the most consistent success, while others saw inconsistent outcomes that the researcher attributes to lacking such a framework, not to the shortened week itself, suggesting measurement systems, not the four-day structure, were the more important factor.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A theater historian studying the long-term critical reputation of experimental plays that broke sharply from the conventions of their time found that such plays were disproportionately likely to be revived and reevaluated favorably decades later compared to commercially successful but conventionally structured plays from the same original era, a pattern the historian suggested reflects how conventional plays, having already fully satisfied the expectations and tastes of their own moment, offer later audiences comparatively little that feels newly discoverable, whereas boundary-pushing plays, often misunderstood or under-appreciated in their own time, may only become fully legible and appreciated once audiences' expectations have shifted enough to catch up with what the play was originally attempting.
options: Conventionally structured plays were more likely to be favorably reevaluated decades later.
Experimental plays were universally appreciated and successful within their own original era.
The historian found no meaningful pattern linking a play's original reception to its later reputation.

Boundary-pushing plays appear more likely to be favorably reevaluated later because audiences' expectations eventually catch up to what the plays originally attempted, unlike conventional plays that already fully met their own era's tastes.
quests.correctAnswer: Boundary-pushing plays appear more likely to be favorably reevaluated later because audiences' expectations eventually catch up to what the plays originally attempted, unlike conventional plays that already fully met their own era's tastes.
quests.hint: Notice the historian's explanation for why experimental plays might gain more from being revisited later than conventional ones.
quests.explanation: Experimental plays were more often favorably revived later, and the historian explains this by suggesting conventional plays already satisfied their own era's tastes, leaving little new to discover, while boundary-pushing plays become more legible once audience expectations eventually shift to catch up with them.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: Since the Reyes family began requiring every household member, parents included, to place their phone in a shared basket by the front door immediately upon arriving home each evening, they say weeknight family time has become noticeably more engaged, though they also observed an unexpected side effect: their youngest child began asking considerably more questions about ordinary household tasks, like how the dishwasher worked or why the mail arrived at a certain time, questions the parents suspect had simply gone unasked before, not for lack of curiosity, but because the child had rarely had their parents' undistracted attention available at the moments such questions naturally arose.
options: The youngest child asked fewer questions after the new phone rule began.
The parents concluded their child had never been curious about household tasks before.
The phone-basket rule appears to have not only increased engaged family time but also revealed a child's curiosity that likely existed before but previously went unexpressed.
The phone-basket rule had no noticeable effect on family time or the children's behavior.
quests.correctAnswer: The phone-basket rule appears to have not only increased engaged family time but also revealed a child's curiosity that likely existed before but previously went unexpressed.
quests.hint: Notice what the parents suspect about their child's curiosity, and what they explicitly say it was NOT due to.
quests.explanation: The child began asking more questions after the phone rule started, and the parents suspect this curiosity existed all along but had gone unexpressed simply because undistracted parental attention hadn't reliably been available before, not because the child suddenly became more curious.
